discussions.strategist:
Today's batch is mostly recycled material. Three items matter.

- Oyu Tolgoi. Mining.com's "begins restarting" headline lands a day after we logged the seismic pause with no duration. If restart is real and quick, it undercuts the margin-story worry I raised on 30 October. But "begins" is not "resumed," and there is no output figure. The 70% export drop from China's border checks is a separate question. Nothing here shows the two touch the same tonnes, so Dr I Simon is right to keep them apart. Yukon's concentrate-import channel stays open.

- Gold. "Gold price slumps to one-year low, silver breaks $50" is the first sharp price move on the desk's radar, but it is a headline with no dated series. It also sits awkwardly with the record. Crux's "above US$4,000" claim is unsourced, and Yahoo reported gold below $4,100 on 28 October. If gold is near $4,000, Harmony's price deck matters more, and it is due in today's 6-K filing. We still don't have it. Separately, the Eldorado Q3 call summary suggests quarterly results may already be out. If so, our 15 November Eldorado prediction could be moot or wrongly timed. Check the release date before scoring it.

- Codelco. An accounting scandal now touching eight more employees is governance, not tonnes. It does matter for Andes Norte, though. A company under internal scrutiny may be slower to publish restart detail, and that cuts against our restart predictions.

- Copper. Nothing here moves the copper view. Highland Valley's strike remains unsized. Capstone's "double production" framing needs a base year before it means anything. The 16 October LME settlement is still unlogged, so the 30 October checkpoint stays blocked.

- Other. Perseus's backup power at Nyanzaga is a gold project, so it doesn't test our grid-attribution prediction. The Iberian Bronze Age copper piece is context, not signal. The AI, uranium and "stocks to watch" pieces are opinion.

PREDICTION: Rio Tinto publishes a company release, filing or operational review confirming underground operations at Oyu Tolgoi have resumed, dated on or after 2026-10-30 | BY: 2026-11-30 | CONFIDENCE: medium
discussions.geologist:
Colleague note, Fri 30 October, midday. Most of today's headlines are commentary or background, so I've focused on the five that touch the record.

- Oyu Tolgoi is restarting. Mining.com's headline says Rio Tinto has "begun restarting" the underground after the seismic pause. That means a start, not a resumption, and it comes from a headline with no company release behind it. It still matters for my channel. The pause only becomes a multi-quarter margin story if it runs long, and a restart under way lowers that odds. It doesn't touch the China border story. Dr I Simon is right that the record still doesn't show the 70% export drop and the pause involving the same tonnes. Until Rio quantifies, the two stay separate.

- Copper is still unscored. The 16 October LME settlement remains unlogged, so the 30 October checkpoint stays blocked. Nothing in this batch fixes that.

- Highland Valley and Capstone. The CIM roundup pairs the Teck strike with Capstone's plan to "double" Chilean copper. The record has Capstone's US$3bn with no capex split or base year, so "double" has no base yet. The Teck strike still has no stated duration or tonnage. Teck's Q3 results, due by 15 November, are the first place either gets a number, and the same filing should give the period and earnings figure behind the "profit surge" headline.

- Gold. MINING.COM says gold hit a one-year low with silver above $50. There is no price series, date or source. Crux's "above US$4,000" claim is still unsourced, and Yahoo put gold below $4,100 earlier. The $4,000 level is the number everyone is talking about, so I'd rather test it than argue about it.

- Codelco. The accounting scandal story, with eight more employees named, is governance news. Nothing in the record links it to the Andes Norte halt or the blockade, and I won't draw that line.

Elsewhere: Yahoo's Eldorado call recap suggests the Q3 release may already be out. Check the release itself for restated guidance and the Skouries figure, since a call summary is secondhand. Perseus's backup power at Nyanzaga is part of the same power theme, but there is no grid attribution yet. The rest (Curzio, ETF Database, the Phys.org copper history, Veramark, the CAMIMEX targets) is commentary or background.

PREDICTION: A named major wire service reports spot gold closing below US$4,000 per ounce on any day before 2026-11-30 | BY: 2026-11-30 | CONFIDENCE: low
discussions.strategist_reply:
Yukon, your restart-versus-resumption distinction sharpens my view. I had been treating the seismic pause as a clean on-off switch, and it isn't one. A restart under way reduces the odds of a multi-quarter margin hit, but it doesn't remove the risk until Rio gives a date and a volume. I'm adopting your wording for the Oyu Tolgoi prediction, because "restarted" is harder to argue with than "begun restarting."

Where I see it differently is on Codelco. I think the governance story can affect Andes Norte indirectly. A company under internal scrutiny may publish restart detail more slowly, and that's a reason to widen the timing window on any restart prediction. I agree with you that the record doesn't link the scandal to the halt, so I'm flagging that as speculation, not a finding.

What I think we both missed is the gold prediction's test. Neither of us named the series. A "published daily price series" is vague about which one, and a single wire-service story can be wrong or stale. I'm moving to your version: a named major wire service reporting a close below US$4,000. Your version is more checkable, and it matches how the desk will actually score it.

On the Eldorado timing, the release itself is the source to check. If Q3 is already out, the 15 November prediction should be retired or reworked, not left to fail on a technicality.

Predictions I now hold:

PREDICTION: A named major wire service reports spot gold closing below US$4,000 per ounce on any day before 2026-11-30 | BY: 2026-11-30 | CONFIDENCE: low
discussions.geologist_reply:
Meldrum, I agree with most of this, and your Codelco point is sharper than mine. A company under internal accounting scrutiny is the one most likely to slip its disclosure calendar. A late quarterly filing would itself be news, so I'd watch filing dates as closely as content.

On Oyu Tolgoi, I'd add a field view. After a seismic event, underground restarts are usually staged, with re-entry, ground-support checks and sign-off area by area before ore flows. So "begins" could mean days of inspection before production resumes. Your margin point only holds if the release says which levels are back. Until then, the export question stays separate, as you say.

Where I'd push back is on the gold framing. "One-year low" is a claim about a price series, and until we have one, "$4,000" is a talking point, not a level. Harmony's price deck is a company planning assumption, not a market price, so I wouldn't use it to read spot. The gold prediction should resolve against a named daily benchmark, such as the LBMA gold price, so nobody argues about the source later.

What we both missed: Teck's Q3 release is the first place to see Highland Valley's tonnage and strike length, and it's a better test than any copper headline.

Restated predictions:

PREDICTION: Rio Tinto publishes a company release, filing or operational review confirming underground operations at Oyu Tolgoi have resumed, dated on or after 2026-10-30 | BY: 2026-11-30 | CONFIDENCE: medium
PREDICTION: Teck publishes Q3 results by 2026-11-15 that state either the Highland Valley strike's end date or the copper tonnes affected | BY: 2026-11-15 | CONFIDENCE: low
discussions.summary:
Key stories:
- Oyu Tolgoi: Mining.com reports Rio Tinto has begun restarting underground operations after a seismic pause. There is no company release, duration or volume figure. The 70% export drop from China's border checks is treated as a separate question.
- Gold: A headline reports a one-year low and silver above $50, but there is no dated price series. Crux's "above US$4,000" claim is unsourced, and Yahoo earlier reported gold below $4,100.
- Codelco: An accounting scandal now involves eight more employees. It is governance news with no tonnage data.
- Copper: The Highland Valley strike has no stated size, Capstone's "double" framing lacks a base year, and the 16 October LME settlement remains unlogged.

Where they agree:
- The Oyu Tolgoi restart and the China export drop should be kept separate until Rio quantifies.
- Gold claims need a dated, named source before they are scored.
- Teck's Q3 results are the first place to get Highland Valley figures.
- The Eldorado Q3 release may already be out, so its prediction needs checking.

Where they disagree:
- Codelco: Meldrum thinks the scandal could slow restart disclosure at Andes Norte and widen timing windows, but he flags this as speculation. Yukon Cornelius won't draw the link, since the record doesn't connect them.
- Gold benchmark: Meldrum moved to a named wire service report. Yukon prefers a named benchmark such as the LBMA price and says Harmony's price deck is a planning assumption, not a spot price.
- Oyu Tolgoi: Meldrum sees a restart as lowering but not removing margin risk. Yukon adds that staged restarts may mean days of inspection before ore flows, so "begins" may not mean production has resumed.
